categories.name: build
categories.evidence: Labeled Windows; addresses Windows-specific runtime socket behavior covered under platform support.
categories.rationale: The PR addresses a Windows-specific socket binding behavior where `SO_REUSEADDR` allows other processes under the same user account to bind to the port. While it provides useful platform hardening for Windows users, it does not fix a platform build failure or crash that blocks the node from running.

categories.name: p2p
categories.evidence: Labeled P2P and modifies P2P listen socket binding options in src/net.cpp.
categories.rationale: Setting `SO_EXCLUSIVEADDRUSE` on Windows prevents a second local process running under the same user account from binding to the P2P port and intercepting incoming connections. Because the vector requires local execution under the same security context, this is worthwhile security hardening that is reasonably deferrable.
